newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen falling on stronger yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen falling on stronger yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to fall in the Monday session, depressed by the strengthening of the yen against the dollar, brokers said, as investors will be tempted to take profits on blue chip issues.
But bargain-hunting may appear near 19,500 by foreign and domestic institutional investors and the Nikkei average's losses could be limited, they added.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average fell 259.03 points or 1.29 percent to 19,802.78. Its June Nikkei futures slid 230 points to 19,830.

The yen surged against the dollar in early Tokyo trade to its highest levels since late January. The dollar dipped below 118 yen before recovering to trade around 118.70 yen. In late Tokyo trade on Friday, the dollar had stood at 123.11/21.

"A correction phase was expected after the Nikkei average climbed past 20,000," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager. "Nikkei futures in Chicago ended on a weak note on Friday and that, in addition to the stronger yen, will be a burden for the benchmark today."
On the Chicagao Merchantile Exchange, June Nikkei futures closed at 19,660 on Friday after shedding 525 points.
